condition: 5. 明瞭度と turn-taking が許容範囲内である
status: PARTIALLY EVALUATED - turn-taking measured, intelligibility not measurable locally

turn_taking.measured_on: the 30 fixed conversations, decoded stereo, channel 0 Moshi / channel 1 user

criteria.speaker_switches: must not be 0 across the 30 conversations

result.control_responds_in: 14 of 30 conversations; 16 have zero speaker switches
result.best: v-real/epoch1, v-real/epoch2, v-real/epoch4, v-tts/epoch1..5 all respond in 30 of 30
result.latency_vs_control: control 23.5 frames; candidates 16.0 to 33.5, all inside 2x
result.verdict: turn-taking is NOT worse than the control for any arm, and better for most

turn_taking.surprise: The control - J-Moshi-ext itself - stays silent in 16 of 30 conversations. Fine-tuning made the model MORE likely to answer, not less. That is the opposite of what the silence finding on the voice prompt sets suggests, and the two are consistent: the voice sets have a silent partner and the degraded arms fall mute against silence, while general30 has a speaking partner and every arm answers it.

intelligibility.why: Generated dialogue has no ground-truth text. ASR against the model's own decoded text stream is self-referential and rewards repetition - a model stuck on one phrase transcribes perfectly. RUBRIC.md's bar is a blind 1-5 human rating, which needs a listener. Neither is available here.
intelligibility.what_was_NOT_done: No CER number is reported, because any number computable here would measure something other than intelligibility.
intelligibility.how_it_could_be_closed: A human listening pass over the adopted arm's 30 conversations, scored on RUBRIC.md's 1-5 scale against the control.

prompt_design_error.what: m3-prompt-sets.json recorded that the user speaks 37-80 frames INSIDE the window [40,165). The census was run on the prompt wavs, where frame 0 is the start of the prompt. generate.py returns only the generated frames, re-indexed to 0, so the 40-frame lead-in is cut off and the user audio lands at frames 1-37 of the returned array.
prompt_design_error.consequence: The user speaks at the START of the generated window rather than inside it. The model answers after the user finishes, which is still a valid turn-taking test and is what the measured latencies describe - but it is not the barge-in-adjacent design the step intended, and the recorded frame numbers in m3-prompt-sets.json describe the prompt, not the measurement.
prompt_design_error.not_corrected_because: The measurement it produced is sound; only the description was wrong. Re-rendering would cost another GPU session.

limits: Partner-channel metrics are excluded as vacuous under --model_user_stream teacher forcing; only the Moshi channel's behaviour and the timing between the two are used.
Barge-in following is not tested: the user finishes before the model starts in every prompt.
